tools.name: send
tools.description: Send a message to a teammate (by name), to 'board' (team pins), or to 'notify' (a one-way notification to the operator; nothing comes back, so never wait for a reply to it). Set reply_to to the #N of the message you answer. Set expects_reply when you need an answer. Another team or a solo session is reached only gate to gate: from your team's gate, send to the team's name (it reaches that team's gate) or the solo's name; see {tool:who}.

body.description: message text (empty only for board op=remove)

reply_to.description: #N of the message you are answering

kind.description: free-form label, not interpreted by piggery

target.description: board only: #N of the pin to replace or remove

tools.name: inbox
tools.description: Read your unacknowledged piggery messages. view=board instead shows the team's pins (read-only, marks nothing as read).

tools.name: who
tools.description: List your team in full (state: idle, working, awaiting_permission, gone), then one line per other team and per solo session on this machine. Teams and solo sessions talk gate to gate only (replies too): write to a team's name to reach its gate; a solo session is its own gate. If you are not your team's gate, ask your gate to relay.

tools.name: agent
tools.description: Manage worker agents. spawn: start a worker (role, name, task; the task arrives as a message that expects your reply, and its reply comes back to you as mail). stop | resume | tail: target = worker name. admit: add a solo session marked admittable in {tool:who} (target) to a role you may spawn (role). templates: list the team templates found can use (summary and roles); read it to pick one. found: create a piggery team from a template (default p2p) rooted at the current directory and become its gate; if you are in a team you leave it. close: close your team (you must be its gate); you become solo and its workers stop. reopen: open again a closed team rooted at the current directory (team = its name) and become its gate; its stopped workers and unread mail come to you. admit, found, close and reopen only when the user asks. A solo session can only use templates, found and reopen.

action.description: spawn | stop | resume | tail | admit | templates | found | close | reopen

task.description: spawn: what the worker should do; resume: optional, a new task for it

cwd.description: spawn: the worker's directory, relative to yours or absolute (default: yours); needs can_set_cwd; must be inside the team root or a git worktree of its repository

target.description: stop/resume/tail: the worker's name; admit: the solo session's name
